# BBK refinement: root continuation, no result

Credit0. Source Banerjee-Bringmann-Keith, arXiv2601.04014v1, Section5 Conjectures5.1 and5.2. Root read actual current HTML Section5 and the prior exact source/partial-results lane. Full nonnegative coefficient statement remains open here; no Lean or paper is warranted.

Put O_r(q)=prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(1-q^(2j+1)). For a=n+1>=1 and b=k-1>=0, the literal source series is

    F(a,b)=O_(a+b-1)/(O_a O_b).

For a,b>=1 this is symmetric; it is the source symmetry, not a new result. If a=1 or b=1 it is 1/(1-q). Previous source/lanes already cover these boundaries; no credit. The source stronger comparison is exactly F(a,b)>=_coeff F(a-1,b+1) in its stated range. Direct cancellation gives, for n>=1,k>=n+1,

    G_(k,n)-G_(k+1,n-1)
     = q^(2n+1) (1-q^(2(k-n-1)))
       (q^(2k+1);q^2)_(n-1)/(q;q^2)_(n+1).

At k=n+1 it is zero. At k>n+1 the residual rational function still needs coefficient positivity; writing it does not prove that property. check_monotonicity.py computes exact integer prefixes of this residual. All1600 pairs1<=n<=40,1<=k-n-1<=40 have no negative coefficient through shifted degree1200. These are finite prefixes, not all coefficients, not a proof, not an eligible finite result. Existing much larger5.1 checks are not recounted.

## Two ruled-out proof routes

1. Divisibility matching: multiply F(a,b) by1-q^L for an odd common period L, then try pairing every denominator factor with a numerator factor divisible by its weight, producing geometric polynomials. At a=b=10 denominator weights are1,3,...,19, numerator weights21,23,...,37 plusL. Neither17 nor19 divides any weight21..37. Both therefore need the single L factor. A bijective pairing is impossible, for every L. This disproves this proof scheme, not positivity or an arbitrary more complicated decomposition.

2. Complete intersection: realize F(10,10) as the Hilbert series of nine homogeneous equations of degrees21,23,...,37 in a polynomial ring with variable weights1,3,...,19. Restrict to the coordinate plane carrying weights17 and19. Every positive-degree monomial involving only these two variables has degree17,19, an even sum in{34,36,38}, or degree>=51 if it has at least three factors. None equals21,23,...,37. Thus all nine equations vanish on the entire coordinate plane, for any choice of coefficients. Their zero locus has dimension at least2; they cannot form a regular sequence of length9 in dimension10 (whose quotient would have dimension1). This specific homogeneous complete-intersection realization is impossible; no conclusion about other Hilbert-series constructions follows.

A still broader invalid criterion is that every odd cyclotomic polynomial divided by1-q has nonnegative coefficients. Exact sympy expansion refutes it already atPhi_105: the prefix sum at degree9 equals-3. This supplies no BBK counterexample because its other cyclotomic factors cannot be discarded.

## Honest remaining gaps

A uniform nonnegative coefficient decomposition, partition injection, or valid analytic/integer-tail proof is absent. The simple-pole/eventual-periodicity facts in the previous lane do not alone establish a sign. An attempted residue-amplitude proof would need uniform control in both indices and a proof of the full initial segment, not just eventual positivity. No claimed novelty, resolution, formal endpoint, paper or acceptance. Do not count the symmetry, cancellation identity, finite scans, boundary cases or failed-method obstructions.

Primary source: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04014v1 . Prior full refinement context: pi-discrete-discovery-r7/FINDINGS.md in the previous campaign. Chern-Wang2601.19845 resolves the motivating sum, not automatically this refinement; root has not independently reread that entire successor in this continuation.

## Further termwise-transformation obstruction

A finite q-Chu-Vandermonde convolution suggests, for k>=2,

    G_(k,n) = sum_(j=0)^n q^((2k-2)j)
      [k+n-j-2 choose n-j]_(q^2)
      (q^(2j+2);q^2)_(n-j)/(q^(2j+1);q^2)_(n-j+1).

This is the usual finite convolution (ab;Q)_n = sum_j [n choose j]_Q (a;Q)_j (b;Q)_(n-j) b^j, with Q=q^2,a=q,b=q^(2k-2), followed by elementary cancellation. It is an identity route, not a positive decomposition.

Even in the source-symmetry triangular range k>=n+2, its individual terms need not have nonnegative coefficients. Take k=n+2,j=n-1,n>=3. After removing the positive monomial shift, that term is

    (1+q^2+...+q^(2n)) (1-q^(2n)) /
       ((1-q^(2n-1))(1-q^(2n+1))).

Its coefficient at degree2n+2 is-1: the numerator has coefficient-1 there, every numerator exponent is even, one denominator part has odd degree, and two denominator parts have degree>=4n-2>2n+2. The positive numerator ends at2n, so no other contribution occurs. The explicit n3,k5,j2 instance was verified by exact integer series arithmetic (-1 atdegree8). Thus a claim that this finite convolution is termwise positive is false, including after the valid source symmetry reduction. This does not refute the full G sum; it identifies unavoidable cancellation in this route.

The still simpler possible assertion (q^2;q^2)_n/(q;q^2)_(n+1)>=_coeff0 is false: n3 has coefficient-1 atdegree12. Chern-Wang's actual denominator length2n in their separate positive theorem cannot be shortened to n+1 without proof. No such theorem is invoked here.

# SUMMARY.md — pi-cauchy-strict-discovery-r1

## Result (one nominated outcome)

`alpha < 1/n => K_alpha in STP_n` for `K_alpha(t,x) = 1/(t^2 + 2 cos(pi alpha) t x + x^2)`
on `(0,inf)^2` — resolves the Simon conjecture (arXiv:1305.1173 displayed Conjecture (2);
MathDB 325521, open). Complete proof in PROOF.md; independent verification below.

## Strongest objection / falsifier

**Objection (substantive):** the proof consumes Theorem 1 of Simon, Constr. Approx. 44
(2016) 103–120 (`f_alpha(xy^{-1}) in TP_n` for `alpha < 1/n`) as a cited black box, and the
Zolotarev/Sato convergent series for `f_alpha` as a classical black box. If either
statement is misquoted (e.g., the published Constr. Approx. version differs from arXiv
v1 — only v1 is public and was read), the proof weakens. Mitigations: the conjecture's
hardness is explicitly about *strictness* (Remark 2(b) of 1412.0132), not `TP_n`, whose
classification is stated identically in the arXiv text, the MathDB record, and the
publisher's page; and the series was verified to ~1e-40 against independent computations
(inverse Laplace; closed form at `alpha = 1/2`).

**Falsifier:** a single explicit `m <= n`, `alpha < 1/n`, and ordered tuples with
`det[K_alpha(t_i, s_j)] = 0` would refute the theorem; the proof shows this impossible,
and high-precision scans (mpmath dps=60, n <= 7, random and near-equal adversarial tuples)
found all minors strictly positive, with failures appearing only above `1/n`
(scripts/check_fast.py, Check 3/D).

**Second objection (novelty):** the strictification mechanism (Gram/Andreief + analytic
non-degeneracy) might be a known Karlin-type lemma, reducing the work to a routine
citation. Screened: no such public statement located (details in discovery.md); the source
itself declares the factorization route powerless for strictness. Residual risk documented,
not eliminated.

## Honest gaps

1. **No Lean artifact.** No Lean/elan toolchain exists in this lane's environment, and a
   literal endpoint is blocked anyway by two source dependencies outside mathlib:
   (a) Simon's `TP_n` theorem for `f_alpha(xy^{-1})` (its own proof uses a local limit
   theorem and Karlin's Theorem 3.2.1), and (b) the Zolotarev/Sato series plus the stable
   Mellin transform and `|Gamma(1+iu)|^2`. None may be silently assumed or axiomatized.
   A literal formalization is a multi-module project (see plan below). **Status: no formal
   PASS claimed; conditional analytic-kernel lemmas alone would not be a full endpoint.**
2. The published JAT/Constr.Approx. bodies were not read (paywalled); evidence is at
   arXiv-HTML + publisher-snippet level.
3. Karlin (1968) and Pinkus (2010) book bodies were not directly accessible; the
   nonexistence of a covering strict-composition theorem is argued from the accessible
   literature and from 1412.0132 Remark 2(b), not from a full book scan.
4. Numerics are diagnostics only, never proof; the ill-conditioning of the Zolotarev
   series for `alpha -> 1, x -> 0` (catastrophic cancellation) limited some float checks
   to `alpha <= 0.6` regimes; the proof itself never evaluates `f_alpha` numerically.

## Literal Lean plan (pinned toolchain lean4.34.1 / mathlib d13f23b7; standard3 only)

Target statement (top level, `CauchySTP.lean`):
```
theorem K_alpha_STP (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α) (hlt : α < 1 / n) :
    StrictTotalPositiveOfOrder (K α) n
```
with `K α t x = 1 / (t^2 + 2 * Real.cos (π * α) * t * x + x^2)` and `StrictTotalPositiveOfOrder`
defined as: ∀ m ≤ n, ∀ strictly monotone tuples, `(fun i j => K α (t i) (s j)).det > 0`.

Modules, each closed (no `sorry`/`axiom`/`unsafe`/`native_decide`):
1. `Andreief.lean` — Andreief identity for continuous `φ_i, ψ_j` with `∫|φ_iψ_j| < ∞`:
   finite Cauchy–Binet (`Matrix.det` expansion over `Fin m → Fin N` subsequences; mathlib
   has the ingredients) + approximation/Fubini over `ℝ^m` (mathlib measure theory).
2. `StableSeries.lean` — Zolotarev series: define `f α x = Σ' k, c k * x^(-(α*k+1))`,
   prove absolute local-uniform convergence (`summable` comparison; the term ratio is
   `O(k^{α-1})`), hence `AnalyticOn` on `(0, ∞)`, and `c k ≠ 0` for `k ≤ n` when `α n < 1`.
   **Hardest honest piece**: proving this series equals the stable density with Laplace
   transform `e^{-λ^α}` (Sato/Zolotarev) — must be proven, not assumed.
3. `TPAlpha.lean` — Theorem A (`f α (x * y⁻¹)` TP_n for `α < 1/n`): must reprove Simon's
   argument (local limit theorem for `X_{α,n}` densities — Fourier/characteristic-function
   machinery largely absent from mathlib — plus the classical `TP_n` of `(y-x)_+^{β-1}`
   for `β > n-1`, itself a Karlin theorem to be reproved). This is the dominant cost.
4. `Gram.lean` — the Gram representation: the Mellin-transform derivation of
   `J_α(d) = sin(πα)/(2π(cosh(αd)+cos(πα)))` (needs item 3's Mellin facts plus Fourier
   uniqueness on `L¹`) and Andreief application.
5. `Strictify.lean` — Lemma 4.1 + Lemma 5.1: analytic zero sets on connected open sets
   (identity theorem propagation), the asymptotic expansion of `det[Σ_k c_k e^{(αk+1)U} r_k c_k']`
   with error `o(e^{(m+αm(m+1)/2)U})`, and the Vandermonde reduction
   `det[z_i^{αk+1}] = (∏ z_i) * det[(z_i^α)^{k-1}]` (mathlib `Matrix.vandermonde`) giving
   nonvanishing. Self-contained given 1–4.
6. Assembly and the `m ≤ n`/`αm < 1` bookkeeping.

Estimated effort: items 1, 5, 6 are weeks-scale; items 2–4 (source reproofs, especially 3)
are months-scale and are the reason **no formal component was started** in this lane
(per the brief: do not invest in heavy formalization before substantive/prior gates, and
the toolchain is absent here anyway). The lane delivers the ordinary proof + verification;
the formal endpoint stays with root.

## Independent verification performed (no second agent; two disjoint methods)

* Symbolic/asymptotic: full analytic proof (PROOF.md), written independently of the
  numerics; the one earlier derivation attempt that failed (termwise series integration
  for `J_α`) was discarded when its prediction contradicted numerics, and replaced by the
  Mellin/Fourier derivation — this trap is documented in progress.md.
* Numerical (diagnostic only): (i) Zolotarev series vs closed form (`α=1/2`) and vs
  numerical inverse Laplace (`α ∈ {0.3,0.55,0.7,0.9}`) — agreement ≤ 1e-33 in
  well-conditioned regimes; (ii) the Gram representation and `J_α` closed form —
  relative error ≤ 5e-6 (quadrature-limited); (iii) discrete Cauchy–Binet/Andreief —
  ≤ 1e-12; (iv) `D_x` nonvanishing asymptotics ratio → 1 for `(m,α)` up to `(6,0.15)`;
  (v) strict positivity of all minors for `n ≤ 7` strictly inside `α < 1/n` (random and
  adversarial near-equal tuples, dps 60), with negative minors appearing only for
  `α > 1/n` as the classification demands.

## Rational algebra and embedding

`MidpointRational.lean` defines the actual pair algebra

```lean
QPoly := Polynomial ℚ
q := 1 + Polynomial.X^2
QAlg := QuadraticAlgebra QPoly q 0
```

`C`, `x`, `w`, `delta`, `flip`, `tau`, and `midpoint` are concrete maps and
objects. `delta` is an additive map and a proved derivation; `tau` is a ring
involution; `midpoint : QAlg →+* ℚ` evaluates `x=0,w=1`.

| Exact interface | Proved content |
|---|---|
| `pair_mul`, `pair_normal`, `w_sq` | Genuine pair multiplication and `w²=1+x²`. |
| `partial_re`, `partial_im`, `partial_mul` | Real coordinate `-q*r'`, imaginary coordinate `-X*g-q*g'`, and Leibniz. |

## Literal triangular inversion and local arithmetic

`OddTriangular.lean` defines

```lean
T f := f + 2*(1+Polynomial.X)*Polynomial.derivative f
TwoLocal a := Odd a.den
```

`twoLocal_iff_odd_den` states the exact equivalence explicitly; this predicate
is definitionally the same odd-denominator predicate used by the root source
module. `twoLocal_add`, `twoLocal_sub`, `twoLocal_neg`, `twoLocal_mul`,
`twoLocal_int`, `twoLocal_nat`, and `twoLocal_div_odd_nat` establish the actual
local arithmetic. Odd division is justified by reduced-denominator divisibility,
not by rational divisibility.

`T_coeff f k` proves the precise triangular identity

```text
(T f)_k = (2k+1) f_k + 2(k+1) f_(k+1).
```

`Bounded N f` means every coefficient at index at least `N` is zero.
`finiteDegree N : Submodule ℚ QPoly` is the actual submodule of degree less
than `N`, including zero. `T_surjective_bounded` reconstructs a polynomial
solution of `T f=B` inside that submodule: at each finite step it subtracts
`T(C(B_N/(2N+1))*X^N)`, solves the strictly smaller problem, and adds the
monomial back. The base submodule `N=0` is handled explicitly.

`T_kernel` uses the nonzero top diagonal to prove the kernel is zero.
`T_bijective` and `T_finiteDegree_bijective N` prove global and every
finite-degree bijection. Only after this existence proof is `inverseT`
selected with `Classical.choose`. `T_inverseT`, `inverseT_T`,
`inverseT_unique`, `inverseT_add`, `inverseT_smul`, and `inverseT_bounded`
prove its literal equation, uniqueness, linearity, and degree preservation.
There is no assumed inverse or coefficient-sequence surrogate.

## Exact general two-row coefficient reduction

For arbitrary n and margins sigma=(s,d-s), pi=(p_1,...,p_n), write an input
monomial as product_j x_j^(a_j) y_j^(p_j-a_j), where sum a_j=s.
The source reads biletters down columns from left to right. Set B_0=0 and

    c_j=min(a_j,B_(j-1)),
    B_j=B_(j-1)-c_j+p_j-a_j,
    C=sum_j c_j.

Then P has rows 1^s 2^(B_n) and 2^C. Q has first row consisting of j repeated
p_j-c_j times in sorted order, and second row of j repeated c_j times.

Proof: before column j, P's first row consists of all its accumulated ones
then B_(j-1) twos. Inserting a_j ones replaces precisely min(a_j,B_(j-1))
of those twos, bumping each to row two. Since row two consists of twos,
these simply append there. The remaining ones append in the first row.
The subsequent p_j-a_j twos all append in row one. The new row-two boxes
record j; the remaining new boxes record j in row one. Induction proves
all formulas, including C+B_n=d-s. This is an elementary coefficient
construction, not a new result claimed for credit.

Let u_1,...,u_(d-C) be the first-row Q word and v_1,...,v_C the second.
The resulting image polynomial is literally

    product_(k=1)^C (x_(u_k)y_(v_k)-x_(v_k)y_(u_k))
    * product_(k=C+1)^s x_(u_k)
    * product_(k=s+1)^(d-C) y_(u_k).

Semistandardness gives u_k<v_k. Thus no numerical RSK or eigenvalue
approximation is needed. A sparse integer product computes every coefficient.
For n=3 the number of monomials is O(d^2); the diagnostics cap degree,
dimension, memory and CPU explicitly. General n is not enumerated.
The direct row-insertion implementation and independent greedy formulas
agree throughout all computed two-row inputs.

## Ordinary spectral reduction and attacks

The source Proposition 2.7 makes A an integer unimodular matrix. Its monic
characteristic polynomial has constant term +/-1. The rational root theorem
therefore restricts rational eigenvalues to +/-1 (Proposition 5.3).
Writing N=dim A, the following are equivalent over characteristic zero:

- all eigenvalues are integers;
- all eigenvalues are +/-1;
- (A^2-I)^N=0;
- tr(A^(2k))=N for every 1<=k<=N.

For the third equivalence use the characteristic polynomial and
Cayley–Hamilton, or Jordan form. For the last, apply Newton identities to
A^2: its first N power sums equal the power sums of N copies of 1, so its
characteristic polynomial is (t-1)^N. Conversely eigenvalues give the traces,
including in the presence of Jordan blocks. This reduction is classical and
is not a discovery. Showing A^2!=I alone is INSUFFICIENT: nontrivial Jordan
blocks may have only the eigenvalue 1.

## Lower-bound potential certificates for the other 31 domains

Let G₁,…,G_k be the remaining nonempty groups and write M for a nonempty subset of their indices. A table L(M,z) assigns an integer between 1 and 12 to each M and vertex z∈V. Its meaning is a lower bound on the number of vertices in any connected set containing z and meeting all groups in M. It is enough to verify the following inequalities:

1. If z belongs to every group of M, then L(M,z)≤1.
2. If z and w are adjacent, L(M,z)≤L(M,w)+1.
3. If A,B are disjoint nonempty group masks, L(A∪B,z)≤L(A,z)+L(B,z)−1.

These are certificate inequalities, not assumptions about an optimizer's answer. They imply the meaning above as follows. Take any connected vertex set T, a root z∈T, a spanning tree, and assign each required group to one chosen vertex of T meeting it. Prune branches with no assigned group, except retain the path to the root. Induct through the rooted tree. A singleton carrying assigned groups uses (1). A root carrying no group with one relevant branch uses (2). At a root with multiple relevant branches, extend each branch to the root by (2), include any groups assigned at the root using (1), and combine disjoint assigned group masks using (3). Each added branch contributes its vertices once; the shared root is subtracted at each merge. The resulting inequality is L(M,z)≤|T|. This proof requires neither optimality of a DP recurrence nor a solver trust claim.
